registry.name: aowlspt official registry
registry.description: Every mod built in this repository, plus the lists that name them. One file with one git history, so a mod list is a document you can send someone.

mods.name: Mod Manager
mods.author: aowlspt
mods.description: Reads this file, resolves it against your selection, and serves the result under /aowlspt/mods so the mod list can be read and changed while the game runs. It is in the registry so that it appears on its own panel and so that nothing reports it as an unmanaged stray; it is in aowl.list.core so that no list can leave it out.

mods.name: Tarkov Emulator
mods.author: aowlspt
mods.description: The game server: profiles, static tables, traders, flea market, quests, hideout, raids. Written entirely on the public mod API, which is the only honest test that the API is enough to build a game server with.

mods.name: MoreBots
mods.author: TacticalToaster (ported to aowlspt)
mods.description: The bot-type and faction API other mods build on. Announces itself with morebots.ready and does the database writing on behalf of whoever answers. NOT SHIPPED ENABLED as of 2026-08-25: it still uses the whenReady("EFT.GameWorld") gate that cannot fail and binds IL2CPP before the Unity thread is live, which kills the client. Meant to be switched on by hand once that gate is replaced with mainThread().bound, the way mods/sain and mods/fov now do.

mods.name: SAIN
mods.author: aowlspt port of SAIN by Solarint and ArchangelWTF
mods.description: Bot AI: layered decisions, per-bot personalities, cover use, searching that looks like searching, squads that behave like squads. A port of the design, not of the C#.

mods.name: FOV Fix
mods.author: Fontaine (ported by savannt)
mods.description: Field of view that stays where you put it, including while aiming and while scoped.

mods.name: SPT Settings Surface
mods.author: savannt
mods.description: Collects every mod's schema from /aowlspt/settings/<guid> and serves one index, so a UI does not need to know which mods exist. The settings surface that ships in 1.0 is built on this; without it no settings page has anything to list.

mods.name: Fallback Settings UI
mods.author: savannt
mods.description: The browser settings page at /aowlspt/ui/page/settings. It reads and writes the exact same /aowlspt/settings/* routes any other UI would, including the per-row and page-level reset buttons, so it is the reference implementation as well as the shipping surface.

mods.name: Admin Menu
mods.author: savannt
mods.description: The cheat/admin panel: its controls are served as a settings schema like any other mod's, so it renders in whatever settings UI is installed. Registered but OFF in every shipped list -- it is opt-in on purpose. It is in no shipped list on purpose: it is meant to be switched on by hand.

mods.name: Graphics
mods.author: savannt
mods.description: Client graphics knobs served as a settings schema. Independent of the shelved native in-game settings work (see docs/SHELVED-NATIVE-SETTINGS.md); registered but not enabled in a shipped list until it has been exercised on a tester install. It is in no shipped list on purpose: it is meant to be switched on by hand.

lists.name: Core
lists.author: aowlspt
lists.description: The mod manager and the game server, and nothing else. What an install needs to be a game rather than a pipeline. Every other list inherits this one, which is how aowl.manager stays in every selection without the schema needing a flag for it.

entries.note: the thing reading this file; see registry/README.md on why it is here and never off
every settings UI reads its index; without it a settings page has nothing to list
the settings surface that ships in 1.0 (browser page); native in-game settings are shelved, see docs/SHELVED-NATIVE-SETTINGS.md

lists.name: Default
lists.author: savannt
lists.description: Core plus SAIN -- the Singleplayer Mod and the bot brains, and nothing else. morebots was dropped on 2026-08-25: it still gates its IL2CPP binding on whenReady("EFT.GameWorld"), the check that cannot fail (fact #141), so it does that work ~13s before the Unity thread exists and kills the client. SAIN's `loadAfter aowl.morebots` is ORDERING ONLY, not a dependency -- SAIN runs without it.
